You must have done it some other way in R?

messages.author: 565fb8e7abc16eb0
messages.subject: Re: Ratio trees
parts:
Hi Dan,

I am glad it worked out!

That graph used read depth from the human microbiome project. The input was an abundance matrix. There was also a separate table that had which samples were in each treatment. If you are starting from FASTA files, the process would be different at the start at least and its hard for me to say what to do without knowing more about how your data is formatted.

The basic process for figure 5 was as follows:

* Get an abundance (number of reads/sequences) matrix of samples vs OTUs that has taxonomic classifications for OTUs.
* Parse using `parse_taxonomy_table`. This will put the abundance matrix in the `obs_data`.
* Calculate the abundance of each taxon for each sample and put that in `taxa_data`.
* Divide each column by the the total number of reads to get proportions
* For each pair of treatments you want to compare, calculate the difference in median proportions for each taxon. I find it useful to do this in a function that makes each subplot so you dont have to add columns for every pairwise comparison to a single table, which would be hard to name columns and parse.  You can also use a wilcox rank sum test here and set any difference to 0 that is not significant.
* Use color to plot the difference in median proportions for each pair of treatments. I log transformed it so that it is centered on zero.

You can see the code for figure 5 here:

https://grunwaldlab.github.io/metacoder_documentation/publication--05--16s_human_microbiome.html

Do you have an abundance matrix?

Zach,

Thanks again. I changed my input files and got everything to work well. Quick question for you. In the function 'plot_sample_tree' should the line

    filter_taxa(sample_1 >= min_count | sample_2 >= min_count) %>%

actually be

    filter_taxa(sample >= min_count ) %>%

Thanks, Dan

Hi Dan,

Nice!

Yea, that looks like it should be "sample >= min_count", unless there are columns named "sample_1" and "sample_2". I think i intended to filter based on both samples, so that they would have the same set of taxa and therefore the same layout, but perhaps I did not filter at all if that expression is invalid, which luckily had the same effect. Thanks for pointing that out!
